newsitem.title: UK: Medeva sees Hep B trial results early 1996.
newsitem.headline: Medeva sees Hep B trial results early 1996.

text.p: British pharmaceutical company Medeva Plc said on Thursday that it expected to announce the results of two key tests of its hepatitis B drug Hepagene early next year.
The company earlier won an important legal victory for Hepagene when the House of Lords dismissed a patent infringement appeal by the U.S. group Biogen Inc.

Medeva corporate communications director Alexandra Hockenhull told Reuters that results of Phase III trials on Hepagene, which Medeva hopes can immunise people who are resistant to other vaccines, should be published in January.

At the same time the company hopes to have the results of pre-clinical trials to evaluate Hepagene's potential in treating chronic sufferers of hepatitis B, which affects an estimated 300 million people worldwide.
Hockenhull said that if the trials on the second indication were successful, this would represent a major advance on current treatment for carriers, which have a success rate of below 40 percent.
Some analysts believe that Hepagene could be an important product for Medeva, which still relies heavily on behaviour-controlling drug Methylphenidate for profits.
Hockenhull said that in the wake of the House of Lords ruling, which is final, Medeva would concentrate on developing Hepagene in the U.K.
Biogen still holds a European Hepatitis B patent, which has been upheld by the European Patent Office. Medeva would be forced to challenge this on a country-by-country basis.
But Hockenhull said "we are not at that stage" and added that Biogen's patent expired at the end of 1999.
She added that the House of Lords' judgement was "a very important statement about the patent, given that people recognise the UK to be tough on patent issues."
Shares in Medeva closed unchanged on Thursday at 264 pence in spite of the patent ruling.
